notes.summary: All-ordinal generated-Psh cone operations and actual ordinary signed test measures, for the full target ambient scope; no Psh-to-CPsh recognition or universal multiplier claim.
notes.detailedSummary: Proves cone closure at every sheafified ordinal successor and limit, so finite continuous generated-Psh differences form a vector space. Builds signed compact Radon measures for canonical curvature and ordinary positive-current multiplier tests with middle-positive decomposition, exact differential duality and retained generic lengths. Lists the complete primary-premise set with versions, LF bodies, hashes and applicability. These are foundations, not a solution of P21.3.
notes.text:
Foundations for an exact original-pair reduction; unverified research draft.

The scope throughout is the unchanged P21.3: K any complete non-Archimedean field, including trivial valuation; X good separated strict boundaryless pure n-dimensional, n>=2; W any ordinary open; T middle-positive ordinary CLD (p,p), 0<=p<=n-1, d'T=d''T=0. D=d'd'', [f]=f delta_X with actual generic Artinian component lengths. This note proves two foundational facts for the new pairwise reduction; neither fact resolves the target.

Let P(W)=C(W) intersect generated CLD-Psh(W), where C(W) consists of finite real continuous functions and Psh is the smallest ordinary sheaf generated by smooth positive-Hessian functions and decreasing sequences, not the class merely defined by current positivity. Then P(W) is a cone containing constants, and E(W)=P(W)-P(W)=span_R P(W) is a vector space. This statement requires no Psh-to-CPsh recognition.

Here is a proof auditing every sheafified ordinal. Rank zero is the smooth positive-Hessian cone. At a successor, two sections are locally decreasing limits of previous-rank sequences. Intersect the two ordinary representation neighbourhoods at a given point, restrict both sequences, and add with fixed nonnegative coefficients. Previous-rank cone closure gives another decreasing representation; ordinary sheaf locality gives membership. Zero coefficients are omitted, avoiding any undefined zero times minus infinity; the constant zero handles the empty sum. A decreasing limit of upper-semicontinuous functions is upper semicontinuous, since its strict sublevel set is the union of theirs. At a limit ordinal lambda, two sections locally have earlier ranks xi,zeta<lambda; on an intersection they both have rank max(xi,zeta)<lambda. That rank's cone property and ordinary locality prove the limit case. Constants persist. Stabilization follows by considering the set of all pairs (ordinary open, ambient function section): a chain cannot add a new pair at every successor beyond that set's cardinal successor. An equal successor fixes all later stages. The stationary sheaf contains generators and is closed under decreasing sequences on each fixed open, so it is the minimal Psh sheaf. No integrability qualification is needed for this argument. Finally finite continuous sections preserve positive addition/scaling. Splitting any signed finite sum into its positive and negative coefficients proves E=span P. No global gluing theorem for E is asserted.

The second fact concerns actual signed measures. For a compact symmetric smooth beta of degree (n-1,n-1), the canonical top-form measure of D beta gives lambda_beta, with integral f d lambda_beta=<D[f],beta>. For a compact symmetric smooth alpha of degree (n-p-1,n-p-1), there is a finite signed compact Radon measure nu_(T,alpha) with integral f d nu_(T,alpha)=<D(fT),alpha> for every finite continuous f. Its support is contained in supp(alpha); lambda_beta is supported in supp(beta).

To prove the latter fact, decompose the compact symmetric complementary test eta=D alpha as eta1-eta2 with eta_i compact middle-positive. Middle positivity of T makes g -> <T,g eta_i> a positive scalar Radon measure mu_i, with finite mass because eta_i is compact. Their difference evaluates continuous f by the ordinary order-zero product as <fT,D alpha>=<D(fT),alpha>. Different decompositions agree on smooth scalar tests by linearity and then on continuous scalar tests by uniform smooth scalar density; they give the same signed measure. Outside supp(eta), the smooth scalar pairings vanish. Density in that open proves that the signed measure vanishes there. Thus its support lies in supp(eta), hence supp(alpha), even if the decomposition supports are larger. This uses middle-positive tests and does not use the faulty general strongly-positive-spanning shortcut. The analogous lambda_beta formula uses canonical top-form integration and the same dual D convention. Nilpotents and nonreduced generic lengths remain in delta_X.

In particular, on a compact C containing both decomposition supports,
|<D((f-g)T),alpha>| <= ||f-g||_C <T,eta1+eta2>.
This controls any locally uniform net with the original fixed T and test. It supplies convergence of products, not a vanishing limit for an unknown multiplier.

Each is stated exactly in its required scope and linked to a versioned primary body, with complete pertinent literal statements/proofs retained in the companion evidence. Complete external premises and primary passage indices:

Premise 0: An analytic space has compact-neighbourhood bases, and ordinary opens are analytic domains with the canonical restricted structure (CLD 11.1.7). A topologically separated pure n-dimensional analytic space, over a complete non-Archimedean field with either valuation, has the canonical calibrated CLD level-n tropical calculus. Analytic-domain calculus agrees with restriction. For a pure closed analytic subspace Y, its integration current equals that of its associated cycle, so actual generic component multiplicities are retained.
Applicability: The target X is separated, pure and good; its ordinary open W carries restricted analytic and calibrated structures. We never replace delta_X by delta_Xred.
Evidence (premise 0): https://arxiv.org/pdf/1204.6277v2, inclusive UTF8 LF 14983-15012; complete literal body sources/cld-ordinary-domain.txt. Unit hashes are preserved in source-manifest.json.

Premise 1: CLD Definition 8.1.1 defines Psh as the smallest ordinary subsheaf of functions with values in R union {-infinity} containing smooth positive-Hessian functions and closed under decreasing sequential limits. In Lemma 8.1.4 successors use ordinary-local decreasing limits and limits use ordinary-local membership at earlier ranks. Lemma 8.1.2 states that Psh is an upper-semicontinuous convex cone containing constants.
Applicability: Only the finite continuous slice is used for potentials. The cone assertion is also proved independently at every ordinal below; no continuity of intermediate approximants is assumed. The locally-integrable wording in the printed stabilization proof is not used.
Evidence (premise 1): https://arxiv.org/pdf/1204.6277v2, inclusive UTF8 LF 9729-9781; complete literal body sources/cld-generated-psh.txt. Unit hashes are preserved in source-manifest.json.

Premise 2: On the support scope of CLD Proposition 6.5.2, every compact symmetric smooth (q,q) form is a difference of two compact middle-positive smooth forms. Its support hypothesis holds for compact support on almost-good analytic spaces. CLD Definition 7.2.1 uses symmetric currents tested against middle-positive forms for middle positivity.
Applicability: Good implies almost good here, and W is good and boundaryless. No spanning by strongly positive forms is used.
Evidence (premise 2): https://arxiv.org/pdf/1204.6277v2, inclusive UTF8 LF 7359-7381; complete literal body sources/cld-positive-decomposition.txt. Unit hashes are preserved in source-manifest.json.
Evidence (premise 2): https://arxiv.org/pdf/1204.6277v2, inclusive UTF8 LF 7918-7981; complete literal body sources/cld-middle-positivity.txt. Unit hashes are preserved in source-manifest.json.

Premise 3: On a locally differentially separated level-n tropical space, a positive scalar current is a positive Radon measure (CLD 7.2.8). Pairing a middle-positive current T with a complementary middle-positive smooth form eta gives its positive coefficient measure (7.2.11). Compact eta gives compact support. A locally bounded Borel function f has the ordinary order-zero product fT, and it agrees with smooth multiplication (7.2.12).
Applicability: Target finite continuous functions are locally bounded. Only positive coefficient measures of middle-positive tests and their differences are used; the broad strongly-positive spanning inference in 7.2.9 is not imported.
Evidence (premise 3): https://arxiv.org/pdf/1204.6277v2, inclusive UTF8 LF 7983-8011; complete literal body sources/cld-positive-scalar-measures.txt. Unit hashes are preserved in source-manifest.json.
Evidence (premise 3): https://arxiv.org/pdf/1204.6277v2, inclusive UTF8 LF 8054-8076; complete literal body sources/cld-ordinary-product.txt. Unit hashes are preserved in source-manifest.json.
Evidence (premise 3): https://arxiv.org/pdf/1204.6277v2, inclusive UTF8 LF 7918-7981; complete literal body sources/cld-middle-positivity.txt. Unit hashes are preserved in source-manifest.json.

Premise 4: Ordinary forms have exterior products, differential Leibniz rules and compatible restriction (CLD 3.3.10–12). Ordinary CLD currents restrict and form a sheaf on locally differentially separated spaces (7.1.6–7). Their differential convention satisfies d'^2=d''^2=0, d''d'=-d'd'', d'd''J=Jd'd'', and <d'd''S,alpha>=<S,d'd''alpha> (7.7.1–5).
Applicability: Thus symmetric Hessians and symmetric multiplier Hessians can be tested on symmetric forms, and the displayed identities are on the actual ordinary open W.
Evidence (premise 4): https://arxiv.org/pdf/1204.6277v2, inclusive UTF8 LF 3769-3803; complete literal body sources/cld-form-leibniz.txt. Unit hashes are preserved in source-manifest.json.

Premise 5: A good Hausdorff analytic space is locally holomorphically and differentially separated. Compact sets inside opens admit compact smooth cutoffs. Compactly supported continuous scalars can be approximated uniformly by compact smooth scalars within the given open (CLD 15.2.2–7). Smooth compact top forms have their canonical finite signed Radon measures; multiplication by locally integrable scalars agrees with integration against these measures (5.8.1–6).
Applicability: The target W has this scope for either valuation. All tests have compact support, so no global paracompactness assumption is added.

Premise 6: CLD Definition 8.1.7 defines CPsh as the smallest ordinary continuous subsheaf containing smooth positive-Hessian functions and stable under uniform sequential limits. Lemma 8.1.8 gives its corresponding sheafified ordinal stages. For smooth scalar f and symmetric doubly closed ordinary T, d'd''(fT)=d'd''f wedge T (8.5.3–4); positive smooth factors preserve middle positivity (7.2.7). The actual proof of 8.5.5 establishes multiplier positivity for CPsh by this definition and uniform convergence.
Applicability: Used to audit what the printed proof actually gives, and for the known smooth-factor consistency check. Proposition 8.1.11's reverse recognition is not a premise.

Sections 12.1–2 define strong currents as continuous functionals on weakly smooth test forms and provide restriction to ordinary currents.
Applicability: These bodies are scope diagnostics only. We do not identify a zero ordinary current with a zero weak form, convert arbitrary generated Psh differences to real PL, or infer positive closed lift and ordinary product compatibility.

notes.summary: Exact ORIGINAL-pair dual reduction: pair-tested weak closure equals exact finite interpolation and signed curvature-relation preservation; failure would yield actual Psh potentials, but no failure or universal closure is established.
notes.detailedSummary: For every fixed target W,T, proves equivalence of the original continuous generated-Psh pair predicate, closure of ambient Hessian test measures in the topology tested on Psh-continuous differences, exact finite interpolation on actual psh tuples, and preservation of every signed curvature dependence. Finite-dimensional separation splits coefficients into two admissible psh functions on the same analytic open. It improves the stronger all-continuous-kernel certificate by retaining original-pair membership, but does not verify the condition for arbitrary singular currents or construct a counterexample. Every-open quantification remains explicit.
notes.text:
Exact dual criterion for the ORIGINAL finite continuous generated-Psh pair class; unverified research draft. This is a formal reduction, not a universal proof or a constructed analytic counterexample.

Use the unchanged ambient/current scope and the cone and ordinary signed-measure results of n1. On the actual ordinary W put P=Psh(W) intersect C(W), E=P-P=span_R P, H={h in C(W):D[h]=0}, and L={lambda_beta: beta compact smooth symmetric of degree (n-1,n-1)}. The map beta -> lambda_beta is linear, so L already is a vector subspace, with no positive-test restriction. M_c(W) is the vector space of finite signed compact Radon measures. Give it the weak topology sigma(M_c,E) generated by evaluations integral e d mu for e in E. It need not be asserted Hausdorff. Because E=span P, it is also the topology generated by evaluations against P alone.

For fixed W,T, the exact original-pair assertion is equivalent to ALL the following statements:
(a) For every compact smooth symmetric alpha of degree (n-p-1,n-p-1), nu_(T,alpha) lies in the sigma(M_c,E) closure of L.
(b) For every such alpha and finite tuple u1,...,um in P, there is ONE compact smooth symmetric beta of degree (n-1,n-1), depending on the tuple, with <D[ui],beta>=<D(uiT),alpha> for every i.
(c) For every finite tuple as in (b) and every real signed curvature relation sum ci D[ui]=0, one has sum ci <D(uiT),alpha>=0 for every alpha.

Proof in full. By definition of lambda and symmetry, H is precisely L's annihilator in C(W), so E intersect H is its annihilator in E. These are exactly original equal-curvature pair differences: every E element is U-V with U,V actual finite continuous generated Psh, and D[U]=D[V] means D[U-V]=0. If (a) holds, evaluation against h in E intersect H vanishes on L and thus on its closure, hence on every nu_(T,alpha). This gives <D(hT),alpha>=0 on all symmetric tests. Since T, hT and D(hT) are symmetric (DJ=JD), antisymmetric tests also vanish; D(hT)=0.

Conversely if a particular nu=nu_(T,alpha) is outside that closure, a basic weak neighbourhood avoiding L is described by finitely many actual functions u1,...,um in P and a positive tolerance. Define F(mu)=(integral ui d mu)_i in R^m. Its subspace S=F(L) is closed: extend a basis to one of R^m, making S the zero locus of the remaining linear coordinates. Since the neighbourhood misses L, F(nu) is outside S. Orthogonal projection onto S-perp gives c=(ci) with c dot S=0 and c dot F(nu) nonzero. Put
U=sum max(ci,0) ui, V=sum max(-ci,0) ui, h=U-V.
n1's all-rank cone proof makes U and V finite continuous generated Psh on the SAME W, without CPsh conversion. For every ordinary compact symmetric beta, <D[h],beta>=c dot F(lambda_beta)=0. Hence the upstairs Hessian equation D[U]=D[V] holds against every ordinary test. But <D((U-V)T),alpha>=c dot F(nu) is nonzero. Thus an EXHIBITED failure of (a) would give the required analytic pair, current and smooth test without changing any field, space, degree or canonical length. No failure is exhibited here.

For a fixed tuple define A(beta)=(<D[ui],beta>)_i and v=(<D(uiT),alpha>)_i. The image S=A(tests) equals F(L). Its orthogonal complement consists exactly of those c for which sum ci D[ui]=0; all symmetric ordinary compact tests are available and the sum is symmetric. Therefore (c) says v is orthogonal to S-perp, equivalently v belongs to S. This is exactly (b). A point in the weak closure gives v in the closure of S; because this finite-dimensional subspace is already closed, approximation gives EXACT finite interpolation. Conversely exact interpolation puts a member of L in every finite-evaluation neighbourhood, proving (a). This proves all equivalences using only finite-dimensional linear algebra, with no current-density theorem.

When the criterion holds for a fixed alpha, direct finite subsets F of P by inclusion and choose beta_F interpolating F exactly. The net lambda_(beta_F) eventually agrees with nu on each prescribed Psh function, hence converges on E. Supports and total variations need not be uniformly controlled; this is not approximation by positive closed currents. If the tuple curvatures D[ui] are linearly independent, S-perp=0 and interpolation is automatic for that tuple. Exact signed DEPENDENCIES are the only possible finite certificates. Their preservation for arbitrary singular currents has not been proved.

This refines the supplied all-continuous-kernel dual criterion. Since E is contained in C(W), closure in sigma(M_c,C(W)) is a sufficient stronger condition. Failure of that stronger condition may only produce a continuous harmonic multiplier, whereas failure of the pair-class criterion above produces actual Psh potentials by coefficient splitting. No equality of those closures or generation of arbitrary C(W) functions by P is assumed.

Every-open scope remains literal: for a global T, apply this equivalence independently on EVERY ordinary W subset X. No extension of potentials from W, replacement of a cover by a basis, or sheaf gluing of globally represented differences is used. The equivalence retains trivial valuation and singular/nonreduced calibration because it only uses the original ordinary products and canonical delta_X.

The indispensable unresolved statement is now exact finite interpolation: for every allowed K,X,p,T,W,alpha and every actual finite continuous generated-Psh tuple, v must lie in the image of beta -> (<D[ui],beta>)_i. Equivalently every signed curvature dependence must persist after multiplying by T. This note does not prove it, nor supply an actual tuple violating it. It adds no verified geometric range to the catalogue and does not solve P21.3.

notes.text:
Source audit and exact residual gap; original P21.3 remains unresolved. This is a diagnostic and a precise remaining-step record, not evidence of a negative answer.

The primary CLD version is arXiv:1204.6277v2 (25 July 2025), https://arxiv.org/pdf/1204.6277v2. Its supplied UTF8 text hash is 64846cb00926267c6238d1afac61b5eaed0a0e3a6349725738f9b1bf163de085. All LF numbers mean raw bytes decoded UTF8 and split('\n'), inclusive one-based lines. Selected complete primary bodies were read, not the whole book. Complete literal statements/proofs, including extraction defects, are preserved in P21.3-primary-evidence.md and the assembled P21.3-argument.md; hashes are identifiers, not mathematical verification.

CLD Definition 8.1.1 (LF 9729-9734) generates Psh as an ORDINARY sheaf by smooth positive-Hessian functions and decreasing sequential limits. Definition 8.1.7 (LF 9797-9805) generates CPsh as a CONTINUOUS ordinary sheaf by those smooth functions and uniform sequential limits. Proposition 8.1.11 (LF 9835-9863) prints the claim CPsh_xi=C intersect Psh_xi for every ordinal xi, but its successor proof has an unprovided inference. Its pertinent literal text is:
"une fonction continue u définie sur un ouvert U est localement limite décroissante de
fonctions de CPshX,α si et seulement si elle est localement limite uniforme de telles
fonctions."
(LF 9841-9843), followed by
"Soit U un ouvert de X et soit (un ) une suite décroissante de fonctions de CPshX,α (U )"
(LF 9844).

The successor antecedent from Lemma 8.1.4 is a continuous limit of arbitrary Psh_xi sections, which can be discontinuous. The induction hypothesis only identifies the CONTINUOUS Psh_xi sections with CPsh_xi. It does not identify those arbitrary approximants. Thus the printed Dini argument handles continuous predecessor approximants after assuming them; it does not supply them. This documents a gap in that proof and does not establish that the recognition theorem itself is false.

The ordinal audit is exact. Base rank zero is valid. Limit recognition follows locally from recognition at EVERY earlier rank: a continuous section locally belonging to an earlier Psh rank can locally use its corresponding CPsh rank, then glue by the CPsh sheaf. No global fixed earlier rank is required. Every successor needs the missing replacement of possibly discontinuous predecessor approximants, including the ordinary covers already introduced in those preceding sheaves. The operations argument in n1 does succeed at all these ranks, but it proves cone closure only, not rank collapse.

Compact upper selection alone does not repair recognition. For upper-semicontinuous uj decreasing to continuous finite u, the increasing open sets {uj-u<epsilon} cover any compact C. Finite subcover gives u<=uj<u+epsilon on C for one j. This works even with discontinuous uj, but does not make uj CPsh. On [0,1], fj=(1/j) times the indicator of {0} is upper semicontinuous, discontinuous, decreasing, and uniformly tends to continuous zero. This is solely a topological diagnostic, not an analytic Psh example.

Intermediate ordinary sheafification supplies variable representation neighbourhoods/covers for each approximant. Fixed-domain transfinite selection omitting that sheafification does not glue local leaves into one smooth positive-Hessian approximant on a common ordinary neighbourhood. An infinite intersection of shrinking neighbourhoods need not contain a neighbourhood. At a limit, finitely many patches have a maximum earlier rank, but still need an actual positive gluing argument. Partitions of unity alone do not preserve Hessian positivity: on (0,1), smooth convex x and 0 combined by positive weights 1-x and x give x-x^2, with second derivative -2. This is a diagnostic of the proposed operation, not an analytic counterexample. No impossibility of other positive gluing procedures is claimed.

The safe inclusion CPsh subset C intersect Psh is independently justified: if finite Psh fj converge uniformly to continuous f, set ej=||fj-f||, choose errors decreasing by a factor greater than three, and fj+2ej has a decreasing subsequence tending to f. If infinitely many errors are zero, use that subsequence. Constants and the Psh cone give Psh membership of the shifted functions. Therefore the continuous part of Psh is a uniform-closed sheaf containing the generators, so contains CPsh. This proves no reverse recognition.

Likewise the literal proof of CLD 8.5.5 (LF 10317-10326) considers the continuous sheaf of f with positive D(fT), includes smooth generators by the smooth Leibniz identity, and uses uniform-product continuity. It ends:
"contient le faisceau CPshX , ce qu’il fallait démontrer."
(LF 10326). This is a valid CPsh multiplier-positivity proof, relying on the ordinary positive-factor and measure facts in n1. Applying it to all continuous generated Psh would additionally need the recognition step just audited. Both h and -h in CPsh suffice for BT: both signs of D(hT) are positive, and compact positive-test decomposition plus symmetry forces zero. But recognizing U and V individually as CPsh does not furnish both signs of U-V. No subtraction preserving the CPsh cone or approximation preserving their curvature identity has been supplied.

GJR v3, 7 March 2025, https://arxiv.org/pdf/2111.05741v3, has text hash 57dfcae1d8dfc25d5ef217f34fabe9e80b679ec2956db1bced3b31bc9afdf8d3. Its LF 339-343 assume NONTRIVIAL valuation. Section 7.13 (LF 2529 onward) defines its psh term by ordinary current positivity, which must not replace generated CLD-Psh. Proposition 10.17 (LF 3367-3386, complete proof preserved) begins with a WEAKLY SMOOTH function and zero WEAK FORM Hessian, and recognizes harmonicity/real PL; it does not begin with an arbitrary continuous ordinary-zero-current function. Its 12.1-2 (LF 3618-3636) define strong-current restriction, without providing the closed positive lift AND ordinary multiplier compatibility needed by this route. No such lift or compatibility is assumed here. The task-granted strict real-PL result, within its nontrivial-valued strict function scope, is not enlarged or counted as a new solution; the fresh missing recognition is for arbitrary original pair differences. Curve function recognition similarly does not restrict an arbitrary higher-dimensional ambient current to a curve.

The new criterion n2 gives the precise remaining universal assertion without using recognition: for EVERY allowed field, space, current, ordinary W, compact symmetric alpha, and finite continuous generated-Psh tuple ui, every relation sum ci D[ui]=0 must imply sum ci <D(uiT),alpha>=0. It is equivalently exact finite interpolation by an actual compact ordinary beta. No proof for all singular currents and no analytic tuple/current/test violating it has been supplied. The catalogue's narrower polycylinder, curve, real-PL, tower, invariant-toric and conditional approximation ranges are retained and not counted as solutions. No generic lengths are discarded and no coarse tropical pushforward is used.
